primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Persistent Mullerian duct syndrome due to impaired anti-Mullerian hormone signaling
mechanism: In a 46,XY fetus with normally differentiated testes, anti-Mullerian hormone from Sertoli cells normally signals through its receptor in Mullerian duct tissue to induce duct regression. Loss of effective AMH-AMHR2 signaling allows Mullerian derivatives such as the uterus and fallopian tubes to persist despite otherwise intact androgen-dependent male differentiation.
vignette: A 2-year-old boy is evaluated for bilateral cryptorchidism. He has normal male external genitalia. During orchiopexy, both testes are identified, and a midline uterine structure with paired tubular structures resembling fallopian tubes is found between them. Karyotype is 46,XY.
lead: Which developmental abnormality most directly explains this patient's findings?
correct: Failure of anti-Mullerian hormone signaling in Mullerian duct tissue
distractors: Failure of androgen receptor signaling in androgen-responsive tissues
Failure to convert testosterone to dihydrotestosterone in target tissues
Failure of luteinizing hormone receptor signaling in Leydig cells
distractor_notes: Complete failure of SRY-driven testis differentiation causes 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis, with streak gonads and female-typical internal and external reproductive structures rather than formed testes and normal male external genitalia.
Complete androgen receptor failure causes androgen insensitivity with female-typical external genitalia; the uterus is absent because testicular anti-Mullerian hormone signaling remains functional.

5-alpha-reductase deficiency impairs conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and therefore disrupts masculinization of external genitalia. Mullerian regression is driven by anti-Mullerian hormone, so isolated DHT deficiency does not explain a uterus in an otherwise normally virilized 46,XY child.

Inactivating luteinizing hormone receptor defects impair Leydig-cell testosterone production and can cause undervirilized external genitalia. This does not selectively abolish the Sertoli-cell anti-Mullerian hormone pathway that is required for Mullerian duct regression.
key_expl: This child has persistent Mullerian duct syndrome. In male fetal development, Sertoli-cell anti-Mullerian hormone binds its receptor in Mullerian duct tissue and triggers regression of the Mullerian ducts. Loss of effective signaling through either the AMH ligand or AMHR2 pathway permits the ducts to persist and form a uterus and fallopian tubes. Because the androgen axis can remain intact, affected 46,XY individuals can have testes and normal male external genitalia; cryptorchidism or an inguinal hernia often leads to discovery of the retained Mullerian structures.
objective: Recognize that persistent Mullerian structures in an otherwise normally virilized 46,XY child result from failure of anti-Mullerian hormone signaling, not from failure of androgen-dependent male differentiation.
clues: uterus and fallopian tube-like structures discovered during orchiopexy

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Persistent Mullerian duct syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes affected 46,XY males as having normal external male genitalia with persistent uterus and fallopian tubes, often discovered during surgery for cryptorchidism or inguinal hernia, and explains that AMH or AMHR2 defects prevent Mullerian duct regression.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: AMHR2 gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — Persistent Mullerian duct syndrome
sources.support: AMH receptor type 2 is expressed on Mullerian duct cells; AMH binding signals duct-cell apoptosis and regression. AMHR2 variants can prevent this signal, allowing the uterus and fallopian tubes to persist while male reproductive organs still form.

sources.title: Sexual Differentiation — Endotext
sources.locator: MALE DIFFERENTIATION OF INTERNAL GENITALIA — Mullerian Duct Regression
sources.support: Endotext identifies anti-Mullerian hormone as the trigger for Mullerian duct regression during male internal genital differentiation.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Androgen insensitivity syndrome
sources.support: Complete androgen insensitivity produces female-typical external sex characteristics in 46,XY individuals and an absent uterus, distinguishing androgen receptor failure from persistent Mullerian duct syndrome.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: 5-alpha reductase deficiency
sources.support: SRD5A2 deficiency impairs testosterone-to-DHT conversion and disrupts external male genital development rather than the AMH-driven Mullerian regression pathway.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Swyer syndrome
sources.support: 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis produces streak gonads with female-typical internal and external reproductive structures; SRY variants are one cause, making failed testis determination inconsistent with formed testes and normal male external genitalia.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Primary Testicular Failure — Endotext
sources.support: Inactivating LH receptor mutations prevent normal Leydig-cell development and testosterone production, producing a 46,XY disorder of sex differentiation with undervirilization in severe disease.
